scope: Four product files and four actual-host/API test files. Source hashes below are scoped final bytes; this is not a whole-tree browser freeze. No game simulation, replay identity, authored content, qualification deadline, or durable browser harness changed.
problem: Solo declared public boot readiness before awaiting its incoming mission-library handoff or checked return. Optional current-mission sharing can add that handoff to the URL before a later reload. A captured profile identifies this incoming branch as the unified-catalog caller. This establishes premature readiness during owned work, not the exact owner of the historical 4,013 ms task.
implementation: RevealLineBoot.reveal exposes ordinary controls as interactive with aria-busy while preserving startup failure ownership; ready alone retains its prior behavior.
Solo reveals before incoming owned navigation, then calls ready only after incoming handoff/exact return settles. Deliberate newer focus and foreground loss still retire incoming ownership.
The inline visibility guard and boot stylesheet permit the interactive state; the native Scene update gate also permits this state so ordinary input and paused preparation can continue.

Boot keyboard/controller navigation yields during interactive state. Loading timer retires at reveal; final ready retires boot resources. Resource/import/missing-ready failures during interactive state restore the inert recovery screen.
The fallback path without RevealLineBoot retains the same two public states. No other native app caller needs to adopt reveal.

broaderFailure.classification: One independent precondition timeout plus one dependent assertion; not two independent runtime failures.
broaderFailure.primary: The paused-cut Versus return case timed out at its initial ordinary Start, before any departure or incoming return. The original five-second bound and original failed full TAP are retained.
broaderFailure.secondary: The parent case then compared a null saved slot with its unassigned expected variable because the earlier nested setup never reached the save step.
broaderFailure.targetedSample: One targeted sample passed the complete paused-cut Versus round trip: 5 passed test counts (parent+4children), 6 unrelated skipped. A diagnostic-only Node loader used the existing waitUntilRunning failure observer, with the same predicate, host-frame pump, and five-second bound. No runtime or tracked fixture mutation was made for this sample.
broaderFailure.limitation: The original Start timeout did not recur. Its cause remains unknown; the isolated pass does not retroactively pass the broader run or establish an environmental cause.

staleAssertionBaseline.finding: An app-only Node loader served the exact committed pre-readiness app. The old automatic-running assertion failed identically:ready,briefing,choose-your-share,paused=true,no app errors. Existing choose launch already requires a fresh Start. The corrected final test asserts that exact briefing before explicitly starting.
staleAssertionBaseline.limits: This is an app-only baseline contrast with the finite native focus mock, not a clean-tree browser run. Its pre-correction assertion included a failure-only existing-state dump; final test source is different.

cancellationAssertions: Held metadata reports interactive, exposes cancellable ordinary controls, and retains aria-busy. Focus/hidden cancellation produces final ready, no open chooser (uncreated is valid), unchanged native first-return at tick0/paused after foreground return, unchanged local-storage bytes, and no focus steal.

diagnosticOverlay.difference: Only await settle(() => h.doc.body.dataset.flightState === 'running') becomes await h.waitUntilRunning('checked Versus return: initial ordinary Start'). Both call the same helper settle with the same five-second bound and host frame pump; the latter adds failure-only read-only state diagnostics.

The broad 111-test run remains failed 109/111 despite the later targeted pass. Boot API counts also appear inside that broader run; do not sum them as unique coverage.

The historical 4,013 ms main-thread task owner remains unproven. This fixes an independently confirmed premature readiness boundary; current browser restoration and performance checks still need a fresh source freeze.
Actual Chromium discard qualification is prepared but has not run. No browser or endurance credit is claimed by this receipt.
